title: SEC7r3: HMAC CryptoCb streaming broken — BAD_FUNC_ARG on every call
description:
crypto2dev_hmac() guards: if (info->hmac.in == NULL || info->hmac.digest == NULL) return BAD_FUNC_ARG;

wolfSSL dispatches HMAC via two separate CryptoCb calls:
  wc_HmacUpdate  -> wc_CryptoCb_Hmac(in=data, inSz=N, digest=NULL)  [hmac.c:925]
  wc_HmacFinal   -> wc_CryptoCb_Hmac(in=NULL, inSz=0, digest=buf)   [hmac.c:1051]

Both calls hit the guard:
  - Update: in!=NULL but digest==NULL -> BAD_FUNC_ARG
  - Final:  in==NULL -> BAD_FUNC_ARG

BAD_FUNC_ARG != CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE so wolfSSL does not fall through to software. HmacUpdate() returns BAD_FUNC_ARG to its caller. HMAC is completely inoperative through the hardware path.

The port was written for a one-shot model (in + digest both non-NULL in one call) but wolfSSL's CryptoCb HMAC contract is streaming: Update can be called multiple times (digest=NULL each time), then Final (in=NULL, digest=buf).

Fix: restructure crypto2dev_hmac() to use the same streaming model as crypto2dev_hash():
- On Update (digest==NULL): acquire pool slot, send INIT+write, store op_fd in hmac->devCtx (a new Crypto2DevHmacOpCtx alongside the key ctx, or reuse a state field).
- On Final (in==NULL): send FINALIZE, read digest, release slot.

The test_hmac_sha256() KAT would also fail for this reason.

File: wolfcrypt/src/port/crypto2dev/crypto2dev_port.c, lines 1052-1053
